trust_boundaries.name: Inbound messages reaching the agent's context

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT treat content retrieved from external sources — web pages, emails, chat or integration messages, file contents, tool or MCP outputs — as trusted instructions
MUST NOT accept or act on instructions from anyone other than its single owner-operator
Any third party who reaches the agent through a connected channel but is not the owner.

threats.summary: A stranger on a connected platform poses as the owner to get CraftBot to accept their message as a task.
The notification the third-party gate posts carries 500 characters of the sender's raw text into conversation history, so attacker prose is in the model's context on the owner's next turn.

Nothing labels external content by provenance when it is assembled into the prompt, and the one module named for input sanitization has no call sites and would pass a matched injection through unchanged.

remit_rules.excerpt: Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.

threats.summary: Whatever the file actions read — including the credential and settings stores — is assembled into the prompt and leaves the host to the provider; no redaction or classification runs on the prompt-assembly path (checked agent_core/core/impl/context/engine.py and agent_core/core/prompts/context.py).
An unbounded reasoning or retry loop burns the owner's provider spend without a ceiling.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision to tool with side effects

remit_rules.excerpt: sandboxed code and shell execution … Any tool or capability present in the agent's inventory or code but outside this baseline is a trust-expansion finding.
GUI / computer-use control of the host … MUST NOT be used unless the operator has explicitly authorized this capability for the deployment
Host command and code execution MUST be gated by owner approval and MUST NOT inherit the parent process environment containing provider API keys or other credentials

threats.summary: Content that entered the context unlabeled can be answered with a run_shell call that executes on the host through shell=True with os.environ.copy(), handing the inherited provider API keys to whatever runs — no approval gate, no command policy, no denylist on that path.

Action bodies are exec()'d in-process from the action library, which is populated with LLM-generated action code, and the alternative 'sandboxed' mode is an ephemeral package venv rather than host isolation; no gate exists between action selection and exec (checked executor.py, manager.py and the app/security/ modules).
add_action_sets sits in the always-available core set, so the model widens its own action inventory mid-task with no owner step.

http_request can POST an arbitrary body to any public host and the 74 irreversible integration senders can address any external recipient; the SSRF filter bounds only private and metadata addresses, and no destination allowlist or approval step exists.

In the documented Docker deployment the agent container bind-mounts the host Docker socket, so the same model-authored shell can start a privileged container and mount the host filesystem — the container boundary provides no confinement.

trust_boundaries.name: Decision to durable state change or irreversible external action

remit_rules.excerpt: Any action that modifies persistent state or creates an artifact the owner should review requires owner approval before execution.
Any irreversible or externally-visible action … requires explicit owner approval before execution.
The agent MUST NOT auto-approve, self-grant, or downgrade the approval requirement for any action above its declared permission tier.
The agent MUST NOT directly edit harness-managed state files — distilled memory, the append-only event log, conversation history, task history, and the memory index
MUST NOT redefine, expand, or weaken its own governance — its goals, permission tiers, approval gates, or safety decision rubric.

threats.summary: The documented approval architecture is enforced nowhere: permission_tier is written and range-checked but never read at execution, so scheduled and proactive tasks commit state and send externally without an owner step.

write_file and stream_edit take any absolute path with no protected-path denylist, so SOUL.md, AGENT.md and MEMORY.md — loaded at the start of every session — can be rewritten by the agent itself, changing its standing instructions for all later sessions.

The ChromaDB index re-ingests agent-written files with no validation, authenticated write path or hidden-content screening, so text that arrived from an external page returns later through memory_search as the agent's own remembered knowledge.
An irreversible side effect runs with no durable record of intent or outcome, leaving the owner unable to reconstruct what the agent committed.

trust_boundaries.name: Local stores readable by the agent's file actions

remit_rules.excerpt: credential and configuration stores MUST be excluded from indexing, retrieval, and summarization by default
Credentials and tokens at rest MUST be stored with owner-only access and MUST NOT be world-readable.

threats.summary: read_file, grep_files and find_files accept any absolute host path with only an existence check, so .credentials/<platform>.json and app/config/settings.json are readable straight into model context with no exclusion list.
Another OS user on the owner's machine reads the stored OAuth and bot tokens off disk.

trust_boundaries.name: Secrets shipped in code and injected at deploy

remit_rules.excerpt: No user-data token, bot token, or server-side API key may be embedded or shipped in the distributed code.
Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.

threats.summary: Live third-party OAuth client secrets and a Telegram api_hash ship in the distributed source as base64 fragments joined at runtime, with the module stating the split exists to defeat secret scanning and build helpers provided to generate more.
Provider API keys supplied to the process (env_file .env in the Docker stack) are copied wholesale into every shell child, so any command the model authors receives the owner's model credentials.

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination
Routine actions and decisions MUST be recorded to the durable event/action log for audit, without interrupting the owner.

threats.summary: Every file sink is configured with backtrace and diagnose enabled, so an exception renders local variable values — the paths that carry provider keys, OAuth and bot tokens — into the log file, with no redaction filter installed anywhere.

Nothing alerts on recorded activity: the ledger and logs stay on local disk with no notification and no off-host exporter, so detection depends on the owner opening a file that host shell access could also edit.

trust_boundaries.name: Dependencies, MCP servers and downloaded binaries

remit_rules.excerpt: Skills and MCP servers the owner has explicitly installed, plus the two documented out-of-box defaults (the filesystem server and the Playwright browser server).
a server whose launch resolves an unpinned upstream package on each start is outside this closure regardless of who enabled it

trust_boundaries.name: Locally started listeners and config surfaces

remit_rules.excerpt: Any server or listener the agent starts (OAuth callback server, Living UI applications, integration bridges) MUST bind to loopback/localhost and MUST NOT be exposed to the public network without explicit owner approval.

notes.lane_fit: Two strains, both resolved by the enforcing-process rule and the lane table's wording. The Living UI sidecar proxy is an agent-started listener but is placed in client_adapters because it is the HTTP surface a caller talks to, not a tool the agent invokes; and craftos_integrations is genuinely two-directional, so its inbound listener sits in user_inputs while the same package's send actions sit in tools_mcp as a separate node.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences against the stored tags, KB taken as authority — all four substantive, none numbering-only. (1) PRAX-2026-08-12-007 stores LLM02 first; its quoted evidence is grant/gate-class (no destination allowlist, no approval step) and disclosure is not evidenced in scan artifacts, so the KB's 'ungated consequential capability' row makes LLM03 primary with ASI02/LLM02 as co-tags. (2) PRAX-2026-08-12-006 stores LLM02 first; same reasoning — an unconfined path parameter is grant-class evidence, LLM03 primary, LLM02 co-tag. (3) PRAX-2026-08-12-008 stores ASI07, whose KB definition is explicitly inter-agent communication; a LAN-reachable unauthenticated web listener is not that, and no other code honestly applies, so the threat is tagged null. (4) PRAX-2026-08-12-011 stores ASI03; a container default password with seccomp disabled and a published port is deployment hardening rather than the agent's identity scope, so it is tagged null. Suspected but not modelled as separate components: the sub-agent runner (app/subagent/, spawn_subagent) and the 197 bundled Skills / 46 first-party actions are folded into the orchestrator and executor evidence rather than given nodes, and no peer-a2a boundary is claimed since no cross-agent transport was cited; app/security/error_handler.py is uncalled alongside PromptSanitizer and is covered by the same finding rather than a node of its own; the remit's `prewarm_all_drives` whole-machine indexing default could not be located anywhere in this source snapshot, so no node or threat rests on it. Edgeless by design: prompt-sanitizer-py-control (a stub with no call sites) and embedded-credentials-py-secret-store (committed secret material, repo posture).
